task: Harden the ED-Finder GitHub-to-self-hosted-Codex bridge so ChatGPT/client-side waiting timeouts cannot be mistaken for Codex/runner failure, and add lightweight evidence for diagnosing actual runner resource pressure. Work from current main. Do NOT access production, deploy, change database state, weaken the repository state gate, expose secrets, or remove the existing 120-minute job timeout/concurrency safety. Implement the smallest maintainable change with tests/static validation where practical. Requirements: (1) every Codex Worker run should leave a durable, machine-readable status/result receipt even when Codex fails; include request identifier/path, mode, GitHub run id/attempt, runner name when available, start/completion timestamps if safely available, final success/failure/cancelled classification, failed stage/exit classification if determinable, and implementation branch name when one was produced; (2) make the receipt retrievable after the original ChatGPT/tool call stops waiting. Prefer a dedicated result artifact and/or non-triggering durable location; do not write into a path/branch that recursively triggers Codex. If using artifacts, use predictable naming and document retention/lookup. If a results branch is materially safer, explain/implement without creating trigger loops. (3) add sanitized lightweight runner telemetry immediately before Codex and on completion/failure: CPU count/load, memory current/limit where available, cgroup memory events/OOM counters where available, PSI cpu/memory/io if available, and disk free. Never print environment variables or command lines that could expose credentials. Telemetry collection must be best-effort and must not itself fail the job. (4) make the workflow clearly distinguish client/control-plane timeout from GitHub job timeout and Codex nonzero exit in its durable receipt. (5) update docs/development/codex-worker-bridge-runbook.md (or create/update the equivalent if the docs PR is not yet on main) with the key operational rule: a ChatGPT/connector timeout does not mean the GitHub/Codex job stopped; GitHub Actions + durable receipt are source of truth. Also document that ED-Finder's concurrency group serializes ED-Finder jobs only and does not prevent cross-repository contention among multiple runner containers on the same VPS. (6) Do not add a host-level flock/semaphore yet because shared mount/container topology has not been verified. (7) Add validation/tests for receipt generation on success/failure where feasible and run git diff --check plus focused checks. Return a concise implementation summary, exact files changed, commands/tests and results, and any remaining limitation that requires host-level visibility.
